text: James Hanley's Boy, published in 1931, was the subject of a court case that began in November 1934 and ended in a trial in March 1935, by which time the book had reached its fourth edition. The prosecuting solicitor, Mr. Jessel Ryecroft, suggested that the cover and the review extracts inside were most suggestive and meant to pollute young people's minds. Boriswood was forced to withdraw sales of the novel as of January 1935, after selling just over 1500 copies in seven months.
meta_description: Boy by James Hanley: a court case from November 1934 to a March 1935 trial; Boriswood withdrew the novel from sale in January 1935.
